summary: The article surveys marriage customs and love legends from around the world, presenting weddings since September 2023 as living expressions of ancient tradition. It covers rites in Italy, Japan, Scotland, Ghana, France, India, Vietnam/Colombia, Nigeria, Ireland and Morocco, along with the legends and symbols behind them. It concludes that customs adapt over time while love legends endure.
one_line: A tour of global wedding customs, love legends and symbols, showing how traditions persist and adapt across cultures since September 2023.
key_facts: In a small Italian town in late September, Marco Venturi and Isabella Rossetti married in the traditional "La Serenata" ceremony, in which the groom serenades his betrothed beneath her window the night before the wedding.
Keiko Sato and Shinji Tanaka held a Shinto wedding in a Japanese village on October 15, wearing ceremonial kimonos and sharing sake in the "San San Kudo" ritual symbolizing intertwined destiny.
The Scottish legend of Isla and Malcolm was retold at the annual folk festival on November 20; Malcolm swam a raging river on a stormy night to prove his commitment to Isla's clan.
The "Lover's Bridge" was built where Malcolm crossed the river, and weddings in nearby Scottish villages include a symbolic walk across it.
In Ghana, Kente cloth is worn by couples on their wedding day and recalls the Ashanti legend of Ama, a weaver who made the first Kente for Kwesi, a warrior leaving for battle.
Akosua Agyemang and Kofi Mensah wrapped themselves in Kente at their wedding on December 3.
Claire Dubois and Henri Blanchard exchanged gold rings in a Paris chapel on January 2; the circle represents infinity and wholeness.
In India, Radha Mehra and Anil Kumar were united by the "Mangalsutra," a black and gold sacred thread tied around the bride's neck, amid Vedic hymns on February 10.
Lily Nguyen (Vietnamese) and Santiago Rivera (Colombian) married on March 5 in a Buddhist temple in Hanoi and later celebrated with a Cumbia dance in Bogota, blending their cultures.
Chinyere Ugo and Emeka Okorie held a modernized "Igba Nkwu" wine carrying ceremony in Lagos on April 7, embracing a more pan-African spirit.
Siobhan Callaghan and Patrick O'Reilly followed ancient Celtic lovers' footsteps on the cliffs of Ireland on May 12.
Amina Kouri and Samir Aziz wed in Morocco on June 8 to the beat of Berber drums.
